info.description:
The Caitlyn v3 API.

Every request is made to a workspace's own hostname, which names the workspace, and carries a
short-lived Caitlyn bearer token, however the caller signed in. The `session` sign-in mode (the
browser cookie) is handled by the SDKs' runtime and is not modelled per operation.

agent, and `Location` names it.

The configuration is that of the entry's `version`, which never changes. Reading the entry (who

agent's version access grant for a version that is not live now, gets the entry without it. It is also absent when that version was deleted
through an older API that does not protect versions named in live history.

patch.description:
Edits the draft with a partial update of its configuration.

Members that are absent stay unchanged, nested objects are merged and lists are replaced whole,
each item taken as sent with defaults for its absent members. To return a member to its default,
name it in `clear`; naming a member that is not clearable, or one the same request also sets, is
refused with 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED`. A draft whose configuration would pass 256 KiB is refused
with 400 `CONFIGURATION_TOO_LARGE`. Returns the whole draft and its new ETag.

post.description:
Publishes a version: live then points at it.

Called on `draft`, it first keeps the draft as a new version named `name`, then points live at it,
so live always names a version. The publish permission alone is enough for both: publishing the
draft needs no permission to create versions, which SaveDraftVersion needs to keep a version
without making it live. Called on a named version, it points live at that version, which
rolls back when live pointed at it before: nothing is copied, and the history entry's `kind` is
`rollback`. Versions never change once made, so live answers exactly as the version it names.

Two publishes cannot silently overwrite each other when the caller says what it expects live to
be: `expectedLive` names the version (or `none` before the first publish), or `If-Match` carries
live's ETag. Either, when stale, is refused with 412; with neither, the publish applies to live as
it is. Returns live, the version published, and the history entry the publish wrote.

these gets 404, so revoking someone's access to the agent stops them chatting in conversations

caller closes the stream. An answer whose stream ended moments before the watch opened may still

nothing; the SDKs use this to re-attach to `SendMessage`, and to reconnect a dropped watch. When
the answer that event belongs to has ended, or can no longer be replayed, the watch sends
`stream.reset` with a new cursor instead, then carries on. Each answer ends with
`message.completed` or `message.failed`, which end that answer but not the stream, so

Deletes up to 100 documents in one call, with a result for each.

Each document is deleted as DeleteDocument deletes one. The call returns 200 even when every
item fails: `results` has one entry per identifier, always in request order, each either
`accepted` (the document is now `deleting`, or already was) or `failed` with a code: `NOT_FOUND`
for a document that is gone or that the caller may not see, or `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE` when it could
not be marked for deletion; try that one again. A document still being processed is deleted like
any other. One failed item never stops the others. More than 100
identifiers, none, or the same identifier twice is refused with 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` for the
whole call. Safe to repeat: a repeat gives the same results, apart from `NOT_FOUND` for documents
that finished deleting in between.

Watches a knowledge base, or one document, folder or batch in it: a snapshot first, then each
change.

Every connection starts with `snapshot`: the thing watched as it stands, its running and recently
finished jobs, and the progress of each document being processed. Then one event per change. A
reconnect needs no cursor, because it starts with a snapshot again; nothing is replayed and
nothing is lost. The SDKs build every scope's `watch()` and `wait()` on this: `wait()` returns once
no job on the thing is running, or raises the error of the job that failed. Events name a document
only to callers who may read it. The server ends the stream after at most an hour, and the SDKs
reconnect.

Starts a planned ingestion batch, and returns the upload policy for the items that need bytes.

`If-Match` is optional. Without it, the batch starts as it stands; with it, a batch that changed
since that ETag is refused with 412. A stale plan is planned again first. Each item's write is then checked and

upload policy: list the items to upload with `filter[status][eq]=awaiting_upload`, upload each to

post.description:
Cancels an Operation's work.

Work not started yet is dropped; work running is stopped where its kind allows. Only
`document_ingestion` can be cancelled today: a cancelled first version removes the document, and a
cancelled new version leaves the current one serving. Any other kind is refused with 409
`OPERATION_NOT_CANCELLABLE`, and a final Operation with 409 `CONFLICT`. Returns the Operation, which
becomes `cancelled` once the work has stopped.

Cancelling needs what starting that kind of work needs, on the same record, which the server
reads from the Operation and checks per kind before it acts: for `document_ingestion`, the
permission that started it (`files.create` for a new document, `files.update` for a new version
or a retry) and the document's readers; for `document_update`, `files.update` and its readers; for
`fill_in`, `reprocess` and `layout_aware_search`, `knowledge-bases.update` and
`knowledge-bases.ingestions.update`; for a `folder_change`, the permission of the change
(`files.create`, `files.update` or `files.delete`) and the folder's readers; for
`permissions_change`, `files.permissions.update` and the record's readers; for
`knowledge_base_deletion`, `knowledge-bases.delete`. A caller without it gets 404, as for an
Operation it may not see. No one permission is common to every kind, so the operation declares
only what reading an Operation needs (`files.read`, as GetOperation), and the per-kind check does
the rest.

post.description:
Reserves a short-lived slot for a file's bytes and returns a presigned URL bound to their
checksum.

Send the bytes with `uploadMethod` to `uploadUrl`, with every header in `requiredHeaders`,
before `expiresAt`; then pass the upload's `id` to the operation that uses it. Files can be at
most 2 GB. For an attachment, name the conversation in `purpose`: the conversation's attachment
settings are checked here, before the bytes travel. The SDKs' `core.uploads.send(file)` does all of
this, and their document and attachment helpers call it for you. Many files at once go through an
ingestion batch instead, which signs one upload policy for them all.

An agent version's configuration: everything about how the agent behaves that a version holds.

The agent's name, description and avatar belong to the agent and are not versioned; who may use

relevance.description: What makes an answer relevant to the people this agent serves, and what it should decline.

definitions.description: A glossary of terms the agent reads the same way every time.

ConflictErrorResponseContent.description:
The resource's state does not allow the request, a unique name is taken, or a request with the
same idempotency key is still in progress. An agent version that live points at
(`VERSION_IN_USE`) or that live history names (`VERSION_IN_HISTORY`) cannot be deleted. A
document still being ingested takes no new version (`DOCUMENT_INGESTION_IN_PROGRESS`), an
ingestion batch with unresolved items cannot start (`INGESTION_BATCH_UNRESOLVED`), and a document
an ingestion batch is working on refuses other writes (`TARGET_IN_USE`); the first and last carry
`Retry-After`. A document whose versions are not numbered yet cannot have one deleted by number
(`VERSIONS_NOT_NUMBERED`).

code.description:
The stable code, for example `NOT_FOUND`. Once shipped a code keeps its meaning and is never
renamed; callers match on it.

What went wrong in this occurrence, written for the integrator. Never holds stack traces,
storage keys or another person's data.

The request's identifier, the same value as the `Caitlyn-Request-Id` header. Quote it to
support.

errors.description:

status.description: The HTTP status code, repeated from the response.

code.description:
The stable code, for example `NOT_FOUND`. Once shipped a code keeps its meaning and is never
renamed; callers match on it.

detail.description:
What went wrong in this occurrence, written for the integrator. Never holds stack traces,
storage keys or another person's data.

requestId.description:
The request's identifier, the same value as the `Caitlyn-Request-Id` header. Quote it to
support.

errors.description:
Field-level problems, one per member or parameter at fault. Present only on 400
`VALIDATION_FAILED` and on the 422 `METADATA_*` codes.

name.description: The agent's new name, 1 to 128 characters.

UpdateDocumentRequestContent.description: The document settings a caller sets, shared by CreateDocument and UpdateDocument.

sourceUrl.description:
The address a citation of this document links to: `https`, at most 2,048 characters. Changing
it needs no processing.

externalId.description:
The caller's own key for the document, unique within the knowledge base. A key another document
has is refused with 409 `ALREADY_EXISTS`.

name.description: The document's new name.

folder.description: The folder to move the document to. It keeps its identifier, versions and history.

clear.description:
Members to return to their default. Also takes `metadata.<key>` and `extraMetadata.<key>`
to remove one key.

UpdateDraftVersionRequestContent.description:
The members of an agent configuration, shared by the configuration a version returns and by the
draft's update and replace operations.

knowledgeBases.description: The knowledge bases the agent searches, and how hard, at most 50, each at most once.

policies.description:
The policies the agent's policy reviews and checked phases use, at most 20. Exported as a
template variable.

connectors.description: The workspace's connectors the agent may use, at most 20. Exported as a template variable.

deniedDocuments.description:
When true, the answer stream tells the caller which documents were withheld from them.
Defaults to false.

clear.description: Draft members to return to their default, as paths.

UpdateFieldRequestContent.description: The settings of a metadata field, shared by its create, update and reads.

name.description: The field's name, as people see it.

description.description: What the field holds, for people.

choices.description: For `list`: the values it may take.

filterable.description: Whether searches can filter on the field. Defaults to false.

givenToAgent.description: Whether the field's value is given to the agent with each passage. Defaults to false.

visibleOnDocuments.description: Whether the field is shown in a document's settings. Defaults to true.

name.description: The folder's new name, the last part of its path, for example `time-off`.

parent.description: The folder to move it into, for example `/people/`.

UpdateKnowledgeBaseRequestContent.description: The settings a caller sets on a knowledge base, shared by its create and update.

name.description: The knowledge base's name, 1 to 128 characters.

description.description: What the knowledge base holds, in words for the people who use it.

agentDescription.description: What the knowledge base holds, in the words an agent reads to decide when to search it.

clear.description: Members to return to their default.

Upload.description: A short-lived slot for the bytes of one file.

id.description:
The identifier the operation that uses the upload takes, for example CreateDocument's
`uploadId`.

expiresAt.description: When the upload URL stops working.

UploadCompletionResult.description: The result of reporting one item's upload.

itemId.description: The item the result is for.

code.description: Why it failed, as a stable code. Present only when `failed`.

detail.description: What went wrong, written for the integrator. Present only when `failed`.

UploadCompletionStatus.description: Whether an item's upload was accepted. Open: new values may be added.

UploadDescription.description: A file described for an estimate, before it is uploaded.

name.description: The name the file will be uploaded with.

UploadPolicy.description:
An upload policy: one signature that lets the caller upload every item of a batch that needs
bytes, each as an HTML form POST.

keyPrefix.description: The prefix every item's `objectKey` starts with.

maxByteSize.description: The largest file the policy accepts, in bytes.

expiresAt.description: When the policy stops working. Renew it with CreateIngestionBatchUploadPolicy.

UploadPurpose.description: What an upload is for. At most one member is set.

agentAvatar.description:
True when the file is an agent's avatar picture: a PNG, JPEG or WebP image of at most 1 MB,
checked when the upload is reserved. Use the upload as `avatar.mark.pictureUploadId` on
CreateAgent or UpdateAgent.

conversationId.description:
The conversation the file will be attached to. The caller must be able to send to it (its
update grant, as SendMessage needs); otherwise the call is refused with 404, as for a
conversation it may not see. Its agent's attachment settings (whether it takes attachments, how
many, how large and which types) are checked before the upload is reserved, and a file they
refuse is refused with 400 `ATTACHMENTS_NOT_ACCEPTED` or `VALIDATION_FAILED`.

UploadStatus.description:
Where an upload is in its lifecycle. Open: new values may be added. `consumed` and `expired`
are final.

ValidationErrorResponseContent.description:
The request is malformed: a member is missing, the wrong type or out of range; it has a member,
filter or sort field the operation does not define; its cursor is not valid for this list; it
asks to delete `draft` or `live`, which every agent keeps; an agent configuration would be
larger than 256 KiB; or a file is meant for a conversation whose agent takes no attachments.

Field-level problems, one per member or parameter at fault. Present only on 400

VersionResult.description: What adding a version did. Open: new values may be added.

VersionSource.description: How a version was made. Open: new values may be added.

VoiceProvider.description: Where an agent's voice comes from. Open: new values may be added.

VoiceQuality.description: How natural a cloud voice sounds. Open: new values may be added.

VoiceSettings.description: Whether, and how, the agent speaks its answers.

voiceId.description: For `cloud`: the voice, from `GET /v3/voices`, for example `Aria`.

language.description: The language and accent, as a BCP 47 tag, for example `en-NZ`. Defaults to `en-NZ`.

VoiceSummary.description: A cloud voice an agent can speak in.

id.description: The voice's identifier, as an agent configuration names it.

name.description: The voice's name, as people see it.

language.description: The language and accent it speaks, as a BCP 47 tag, for example `en-NZ`.

WatchConversationOutputPayload.description: The rest of the answer, as a stream of `ConversationEvent` events.

WatchKnowledgeBaseOutputPayload.description: The events, as a stream of `KnowledgeBaseEvent` events.
